title: Describir una rutina real
communication_goal: Describir hábitos afirmativos y negativos de forma conectada, comprensible y personal.
situation: Presentas tu rutina y comparas tus hábitos con los de otra persona.

vocabulary.example: I don't relax in the morning.
We take a break at noon.
I don't have much free time.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: I work on weekdays, but I don't work on Sundays.
dialogue.spanish: Trabajo entre semana, pero no trabajo los domingos.

dialogue.speaker: David
dialogue.english: I don't work on Sundays either. I prepare breakfast for my family.
dialogue.spanish: Yo tampoco trabajo los domingos. Preparo el desayuno para mi familia.

dialogue.speaker: David
dialogue.english: Yes, they do. We usually eat at eight.
dialogue.spanish: Sí. Normalmente comemos a las ocho.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.english: My family doesn't eat together because our schedules are different.
dialogue.spanish: Mi familia no come junta porque nuestros horarios son diferentes.

explanation_es: Para hablar con naturalidad combina afirmaciones y negaciones: I work, but I don't work on Sundays. Usa and para añadir, but para contrastar y because para explicar una razón. En tercera persona: She prepares breakfast, but she doesn't work on Sundays.
spanish_speaker_notes: No conviertas cada frase en una traducción aislada; conecta ideas con and, but y because.
Recuerda: he/she + verbo con s en afirmativa, pero he/she + doesn't + verbo base en negativa.
Either al final puede significar 'tampoco' en una oración negativa.
La precisión importa, pero una rutina simple y comprensible es mejor que una frase larga con muchos errores.

targets.text: I work on weekdays, but I don't work on Sundays.
She prepares breakfast, but she doesn't work on Sundays.
targets.focus: s de prepares y verbo base después de doesn't

pronunciation.tip_es: Marca el contraste con la voz, no con pausas excesivas: afirmación, but, negación.

reading.title: A balanced week
reading.text: David works on weekdays, but he doesn't work on Sundays. He prepares breakfast and eats with his family. Sara works too, but her family doesn't eat together because their schedules are different. On weekends, Sara relaxes and David visits his parents.
